intro.say: Let's meet two busy helpers in your chest: your heart and your lungs!

rounds.say: Your heart is in your chest. It goes thump, thump all day and night! Put your hand on your chest to feel it.
rounds.caption: My heart beats

rounds.say: Your lungs fill up with air when you breathe in, and empty when you breathe out. Like two balloons!
rounds.caption: Breathe in, breathe out

options.label: In your foot
options.why: Your heart is much higher up.

rounds.explain: Your heart is inside your chest, behind your ribs.

rounds.ask: What do your lungs help you do?

options.label: Eat
options.why: Eating uses your mouth and tummy.

rounds.explain: Lungs help us breathe air in and out.

rounds.ask: What sound does a heart make?
rounds.explain: A heartbeat sounds like thump, thump.

options.label: Water
options.why: We can't breathe water like fish.

rounds.explain: We breathe in air through our nose and mouth.

rounds.ask: Is it about the heart or the lungs?
rounds.explain: Hearts beat and pump blood, lungs breathe air.

intro.say: Your heart is a pump, and your lungs collect something your body needs!

rounds.say: Your heart is a muscle that pumps blood all around your body, through tubes called blood vessels.
rounds.caption: Heart pumps blood

rounds.say: When you breathe in, your lungs take oxygen from the air. Your blood carries the oxygen to every part of you.
rounds.caption: Air → lungs → blood

rounds.explain: The heart pumps blood all around your body.

rounds.ask: Your heart is a kind of what?

options.label: Bone
options.why: The heart is not a bone.

rounds.explain: Your heart is a strong muscle that squeezes again and again.

rounds.ask: What do your lungs take from the air?

options.label: Sugar
options.why: There is no sugar in air.

options.label: Juice
options.why: Air has no juice in it.

rounds.explain: Your lungs take oxygen from the air, and your body needs it.

rounds.ask: What happens to your heartbeat when you run fast?
rounds.explain: Your muscles need more oxygen, so your heart beats faster.

rounds.ask: Put the breathing journey in order.
rounds.explain: Air goes in your nose to your lungs, then blood carries oxygen to your muscles.

intro.say: Let's investigate heartbeats and breathing like real scientists!

rounds.say: Doctors listen to your heart with a stethoscope. A resting child's heart beats about 90 times a minute. Running makes it much faster!
rounds.caption: Rest: slow · Run: fast

rounds.say: You breathe in oxygen and breathe out a gas called carbon dioxide. Exercise makes your heart and lungs stronger.
rounds.caption: In: oxygen · Out: carbon dioxide

rounds.ask: What tool does a doctor use to listen to your heart?
rounds.explain: A stethoscope lets the doctor hear your heartbeat.

rounds.ask: Which shows a heart after running a race?

options.label: Very slow
options.why: After a race your heart is fast, not slow.

rounds.explain: After running, your heart beats fast to send more oxygen.

options.label: Food
options.why: Food does not come out when we breathe.

rounds.explain: We breathe out carbon dioxide, a gas our body does not need.

rounds.ask: Why do you breathe faster when you exercise?
rounds.explain: Working muscles need extra oxygen, so you breathe faster.

rounds.ask: Which helps keep your heart and lungs healthy?

options.label: Sitting all day
options.why: Hearts need exercise to stay strong.

options.label: Only fried food
options.why: Too much fried food is not good for hearts.

rounds.explain: Fresh air, exercise and never smoking keep hearts and lungs healthy.

rounds.ask: Would your heart beat fast or slow?
rounds.explain: Active play makes your heart speed up, resting slows it down.
